title: Panch Parmeshwar
text:
Jumman Shaikh and Algu Chaudhari were the closest of friends in their village in northern India. Jumman's elderly aunt had signed her property over to him on the promise that he would look after her. Once he had it, he and his wife made her life miserable. At last she called a panchayat, the village council, to settle the matter. To Jumman's delight, she asked Algu to serve as the head judge.

Algu was reluctant. The aunt asked him whether he would refuse to speak the truth for fear of losing a friend. Seated as the judge, Algu examined the case honestly and ruled against Jumman: he must give his aunt a monthly allowance or return her property. Jumman was furious, and the friendship ended. He waited for his revenge.

Some time later Algu sold one of his bullocks to a carter, Samjhu Sahu, on credit. Samjhu worked the animal mercilessly until it dropped dead, then refused to pay. Algu took the dispute to the panchayat, and Samjhu chose Jumman as head judge, sure that he would punish his old friend.

But once Jumman sat in the judge's seat, he felt its weight. He set aside his grudge and ruled that Samjhu must pay. Algu embraced him, and Jumman understood that the voice of the panch is the voice of God.
lesson: When you are given the role of judge, your loyalties and grudges must step outside the room. People accept hard decisions from someone they know will be fair even to a friend.
people: Jumman Shaikh, Algu Chaudhari, Jumman's aunt, Samjhu Sahu
